'''''Algebra''''' is a [[Postgraduate education|graduate-level]] textbook on [[abstract algebra]] written by [[Serge Lang]] and was originally published by [[Addison-Wesley]] in 1965. Its intended audience is students in graduate-level courses and readers who have previously attended undergraduate-level algebra courses.{{r|third}}

==Topics==
The third edition is divided into four parts.{{r|third}} 
*The first part, ''The Basic Objects of [[Algebra]]'', covers [[Group (mathematics)|groups]], [[Ring (mathematics)|rings]], [[Module (mathematics)|modules]], and [[polynomial]]s. 
*The second part, ''Algebraic Equations'', focuses on [[Field (mathematics)|field theory]] and includes a chapter on [[Noetherian ring]]s and [[Noetherian module|modules]]. 
*The third part, ''[[Linear algebra|Linear Algebra]] and Representations'', contains chapters on the [[tensor product]] of modules and [[semi-simplicity]]. 
*The fourth part, ''[[Homological algebra|Homological Algebra]]'', covers [[Homology (mathematics)|general homology theory]] and finite free [[Resolution (algebra)|resolutions]].

==Audience and reception==
The [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) strongly recommends that undergraduate mathematics libraries have a copy of Lang's ''Algebra'' available.{{r|maa}}

Reviews of ''Algebra'' appeared in ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]'' in 1967 and 2003.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brandstein |first1=A. G. |last2=Lang |first2=Serge |date=January 1967 |title=Algebra. |url=https://doi.org/10.2307/2314094 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=74 |issue=1 |pages=103 |doi=10.2307/2314094 |jstor=2314094 |issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Leversha |first=Gerry |date=July 2003 |title=Algebra, by Serge Lang. Pp. 914. £52.50 (hbk). 2002. ISBN 0 387 95385 X (Springer-Verlag). |url=https://doi.org/10.1017/s0025557200173310 |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=87 |issue=509 |pages=390–391 |doi=10.1017/s0025557200173310 |issn=0025-5572|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Professor [[George Bergman]] of [[University of California, Berkeley]] wrote ''Companion to Lang's Algebra'', a 222-page book of notes collected when teaching Berkeley's basic graduate algebra course from Lang’s book.{{r|bergman}}
